video_title: The $114 Trillion Question: How DTCC Is Tokenizing the Entire U.S. Market
gist: Nadeen/Naen Chakar, managing director and global head of DTCC digital assets, walks through DTCC's July 15 production tokenization event, in which real DTC-custodied shares were converted into tokens on the Besu and Canton chains, traded with CME, NYSE and NASDAQ in the loop, and converted back. He frames the October go-live as a scope-limited launch governed by a December 2025 SEC no-action letter covering Russell 1000 underliers, index ETFs, treasuries and some fixed income, and argues that adoption will be slow and measured, driven by collateral and intraday repo use cases rather than press releases.

insights.claim: DTCC executed real production trades on July 15 in which shares held at the Depository Trust Company were converted into tokens, moved into wallets, and converted back into traditional form, with DTCC participants, their clients, CME as clearing house, and the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ as execution venues all in the loop.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Tokenization of US equities has crossed from pilot to live plumbing with the official recordkeeper at the center, which pulls forward the timeline for institutional digital-asset infrastructure vendors and chain operators.
insights.quote: It wasn't a fake trade, right? Like actually shares moved. They became digital. They were deposited in a wallet and then deposited back in traditional form.

insights.claim: DTCC safekeeps 1.4 million CUSIPs worth $114 trillion, and the July event converted only a subset of that book into digital format.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Sizes the total addressable pool for on-chain US securities collateral and sets the denominator against which any early tokenized volume should be judged.
insights.quote: We safekeep 1.4 million QIPS that are worth $114 trillion.

insights.claim: The July event covered seven or eight trade varieties including posting central counterparty margin, collateral trades, simple equity conversions, equity versus payment, and a cross-chain transfer of assets between the Besu and Canton networks and back.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Cross-chain movement of DTCC-recorded securities means chain choice need not be a lock-in decision, reducing winner-take-all odds for any single institutional chain.

insights.claim: The regulatory unlock for DTCC's tokenization program was an SEC no-action letter received in December 2025, which followed years of prior work and defines exactly what DTCC can and cannot tokenize.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: The no-action letter, published on DTCC's website, is the binding document for anyone modeling the pace and scope of US securities tokenization.

themes.theme: Digital twins and the good control location

insights.claim: DTCC's tokens are conversions rather than new instruments: the digital and traditional versions share the same CUSIP, are fungible, and carry the same investor protections including dividend payment and voting rights, with DTCC remaining custodian and official recordkeeper throughout.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: A same-CUSIP conversion model means tokenized US equities should not trade at a structural discount or premium to their traditional form, unlike wrapper-based tokenization schemes.

insights.claim: The SEC has published a definition of four or five distinct tokenization models ranked by where legal ownership sits, and DTCC positions its own model as the one anchored in its role as the good control location and official recordkeeper of the United States.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Gives investors a taxonomy for triaging tokenization ventures: models where ownership sits away from the control location carry different legal and credit risk.

insights.claim: Avoiding liquidity fragmentation was an explicit design constraint for DTCC, which built conversion so participants can sit in whichever liquidity pool (traditional or digital) suits them at a given moment rather than being forced into a separate tokenized market.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Competing tokenization venues that create isolated digital order books face a structural liquidity disadvantage against DTCC's convertible model.

insights.claim: Chakar argues recursive tokenization is the core systemic risk of the tokenized market and that intermediation is therefore a feature rather than a defect, since without a control location no one can verify what actually backs a token.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: A direct counter to the disintermediation thesis; flags backing-verification as the diligence question for any tokenized real-world-asset exposure.
insights.quote: You tokenize a token and somebody could tokenize it and tokenize it. How do you know at the end of the day what's backing these tokens? So a lot of people think intermediation is a bad thing. I don't believe it is.

themes.theme: October launch scope and SEC guardrails

insights.claim: The SEC no-action letter authorizes DTCC to tokenize the underlying holdings of the Russell 1000, ETFs linked to major indices, treasuries, and certain fixed income instruments, so the full $114 trillion will not be tokenizable at launch.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Defines the exact eligible asset universe for the first wave of DTCC tokenization, which is where early on-chain collateral and repo activity will concentrate.
insights.quote: it authoriz us to tokenize all the under under uh line holdings of the Russell 1000 so 1000 equities um in the United States

insights.claim: A key purpose of running July before the October launch was to force clients to confront the operational rebuild tokenization requires, since an always-on economy breaks existing middle office, back office, risk model and trading function assumptions.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Institutional readiness, not DTCC capacity, is the binding constraint on tokenized volume, which favors vendors selling 24/7 middle- and back-office and risk infrastructure.
insights.quote: you're sort of now starting to inch into an always on economy and your your middle, your back office, your risk models, uh your trading functions

insights.claim: DTCC set up client working groups within its digital group in early spring specifically to collect feedback and make the platform usable beyond DTCC's own assumptions, and will open test environments to clients shortly before go-live.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Test-environment participation ahead of October is an observable early read on which institutions are genuinely ready to transact.

themes.theme: Adoption pace and where demand is real

insights.claim: Chakar expects October volumes to be slow and measured rather than a rush, explicitly declining to forecast participant counts and saying he does not expect institutions to be queueing to get in on day one.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Tempers expectations for a visible volume spike at launch; disappointing early prints should not be read as failure of the model.
insights.quote: I'm not I don't think that there'll be a line uh of of institutions like clamoring to get in.

insights.claim: The strongest institutional demand DTCC is seeing is in collateral trades and intraday repo, where settlement speed converts directly into money.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Collateral mobility and intraday repo are the first tokenization use cases with genuine P&L, making them the highest-signal area to track for real volume.
insights.quote: in any type of trades where speed is important, right? Because speed is money.

insights.claim: A new breed of quasi-fintech financial services providers such as Alpaca and Velocity are transacting on DTCC digital rails side by side with JP Morgan, Goldman and Citadel, rather than the platform being the preserve of incumbents.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Fintech brokerages get parity access to tokenized US securities infrastructure, which narrows the distribution moat of bulge-bracket firms.
insights.quote: there's a new breed of providers the alpacas of the world uh that are out there velocity uh and they're doing this side by side with the likes of JP Morgan and Goldman and Citadel and so on

insights.claim: Chakar says the era of tokenizing for the press release is over and that institutions are now tokenizing for purpose because it adds value to their environments.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: A filter for evaluating tokenization announcements: ask whether the trade recurs in the client's daily book or was a one-off demonstration.
insights.quote: people are just not going to do this so they can issue a press release. They're going to do this because it adds value to their environments.

insights.claim: DTCC is explicitly not entering collateral management as a business and is instead providing shared blockchain infrastructure on which agents, lenders and participants move and finance their own assets.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Incumbent collateral managers and tri-party agents are not being disintermediated by DTCC, which changes the competitive read on that segment.
insights.quote: I want to be very clear DTCC is not engaging in collateral management. We're providing shared blockchain infrastructure

insights.claim: DTCC is deliberately deferring atomic settlement and other frequently requested features, sequencing them by client feedback under a do-no-harm constraint given the depth and efficiency of existing US markets.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Instant atomic settlement of US equities is not on the near-term roadmap, so theses depending on T+0 settlement mechanics should be pushed out.

insights.claim: DTCC expects traditional and digital assets to coexist for a long period rather than a full migration, with DTCC obliged to service both at the same standard of care and clients bearing the integration burden on their side.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Dual-rail operation for years means sustained cost, not immediate savings, for market participants and steady demand for integration work.

insights.claim: Besu is a chain DTCC has run internally for years and Canton was simply DTCC's first partner because clients wanted Canton and its privacy approach appeals to financial institutions, so the use of permissioned-style chains was not a deliberate anti-public-chain strategy.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Canton's early lead is a path-dependent client-demand artifact rather than a durable architectural endorsement, so its position is contestable.

insights.claim: DTCC has publicly committed to Stellar as a chain but Stellar will not be part of the October launch and is slated for 2027, with additional chains to be announced in coming weeks and months.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Concrete timing correction for anyone pricing Stellar on near-term DTCC integration: the catalyst is 2027, not October.
insights.quote: No, we've said it would uh it will happen in 2027.

insights.claim: Chakar argues the public-versus-private chain debate is splitting hairs and irrelevant to DTCC, since selection is driven by safety, security, privacy for billions of sensitive transactions, sufficient liquidity, and client demand rather than decentralization purity.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Institutional chain selection will reward privacy and operational assurance over permissionlessness, disadvantaging chains whose pitch is decentralization alone.
insights.quote: whether it's private or public doesn't really matter. What's matter is that it's safe and secure

insights.claim: Canton's decentralization status is genuinely contested: Chakar calls it public wrapped with privacy because no single entity controls it, while the host notes its validators are permissioned through a Canton Foundation approval process unlike Bitcoin or Ethereum.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar and host
insights.so_what: The contested definition matters for regulatory and decentralization risk assessments of Canton-hosted tokenized securities.
insights.quote: Canton is not private uh but it's public wrapped with privacy

themes.theme: Incumbent absorbs crypto: the disruption reframe

insights.claim: Chakar accepts that crypto technology did disrupt DTCC, but says DTCC responded by acquiring a firm for its technology knowhow and taking the best of Bitcoin and Ethereum to extend its own franchise, describing it as DTCC disrupting itself.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: The incumbent-absorption path means blockchain value accrues to infrastructure and incumbents rather than to protocols positioned as their replacements.
insights.quote: we've disrupted ourselves thanks to the new technology that's come in, but we will do this responsibly. We're not looking to rip the old and put the new in place.

insights.claim: Chakar attributes the crypto revolution mainly to retail rather than institutions, and says institutional participation required certainty in both regulation and the technology before it could move.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Regulatory certainty is the gating variable for institutional crypto capital, so rule-making milestones matter more than technical ones for flows.
insights.quote: this whole crypto revolution was really driven more by retail than it was on the institutional side

insights.claim: Chakar claims July 15 would not have happened without DTCC leading, and predicts the DTCC of the next 55 years will look very different from the DTCC of the past 55 years as the technology, infrastructure and new regulations change how firms work holistically.
insights.speaker: Naen Chakar, DTCC global head of digital assets
insights.so_what: Signals a structural business-model shift at the market's central utility, with knock-on effects for custodians, brokers and clearing intermediaries whose functions it may absorb or reshape.
insights.quote: the DTCC of the next 55 years is going to look a lot different from the DTCC of the past 55 years
